title: AniRec
one_liner: Find your next anime from the shows you enjoy and recommendations from other viewers.
short_description: Select one or more anime and browse recommendations drawn from MyAnimeList community connections. AniRec balances the selected shows, groups linked seasons, and keeps related films separate.

project_page_hero.headline: AniRec
project_page_hero.subhead: Turn the anime you enjoy into a collection of recommendations.

portfolio_framing.overview: AniRec searches MyAnimeList on demand and turns one or more selections into ranked poster cards. Title popups expose available metadata, individual ratings, seasons, and related films.
portfolio_framing.archive_link_box: Live AniRec application, reproducible source, and verification.

input_process_output.input: Selected MAL anime IDs, community recommendation counts, release relationships, and available title metadata.
input_process_output.process: Normalize each release list, resolve verified show identities, combine equal-weight support across unique selected shows, and rank deterministically.
input_process_output.output: Responsive poster cards, ten-at-a-time results, detailed popups, individually rated seasons and separately listed films.

overview_highlights: Live official MAL search and metadata.
Equal influence across unique selected shows with overlap-sensitive ranking.
Seasons and parts grouped; related films remain independent.
Poster grid and details work on desktop and mobile.
detail_sections.how_it_works_summary: Choose anime you enjoy, explore the ranked connections, and open a card to learn more.
how_it_works_steps: Search and select one to eight titles.
Resolve linked seasons into shows and normalize the returned community recommendation counts.
Combine support using the square of the mean square root of normalized support.
Show ten cards initially, then reveal ten more until the returned candidates are exhausted.
Open details for synopsis, available metadata, season ratings and related movies.
detail_sections.technical_summary: React, TypeScript and Radix Dialog provide the interface. Node.js and Express keep MAL credentials on the server. Bounded caches, in-flight deduplication and request limits reduce repeated work and expose service failures. Vite and Vercel deliver the application.
detail_sections.evidence_summary: 147 automated tests pass. A live two-show check matched all 43 ranked IDs and scores between the clean export and public app. Browser checks exercised paging and actual title/franchise details.

evidence.claim: Multi-title ranking preserves equal influence and deterministic order.
evidence.evidence: Synthetic normalization, duplicate-season, ordering and overlap tests pass; the live two-show comparison matched all 43 IDs and scores.

evidence.claim: The interface exposes real community-backed recommendations and franchise details.
evidence.evidence: Literal production-build captures and public browser checks show ranked cards, title facts, two Code Geass seasons and three related films.

limitations: Results are limited to the recommendations and metadata returned by MyAnimeList.
Missing artwork, synopsis or ratings remain unavailable.
MAL does not provide a canonical show ID; ambiguous or unusually large relationship graphs can return recoverable errors.
Provider latency, rate limits and availability remain external dependencies.
claim_boundaries: The score is relative community support, not a probability of enjoyment or measured recommendation accuracy.
The application uses deterministic scoring and no trained recommendation model.
Screenshots document a specific source commit and live metadata snapshot; data and rankings may change.
Anime artwork and MAL content belong to their respective rights holders; source publication grants no rights to those materials.
